value: US EPA Office of Air and Radiation (2010). Available and Emerging Technologies for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions from the Pulp and Paper Manufacturing Industry. Prepared by the Sector Policies and Programs Division, Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Research Triangle Park, NC, October 2010.

Loaded (main file): whole technologies with their own cost or performance - low- and high-temperature black liquor gasification (installed capex, 6 million lb BLS/day, Larson 2003), Tomlinson recovery furnace efficiency range, heat-to-power ratios derived from the printed E/T ratios for boiler/steam-turbine, simple-cycle and combined-cycle CHP, a combined-cycle case (92 MW for $75 million, availability >95%), back-pressure PRV-replacement turbine ($600/kWe, $0.011/kWh O&M), STIG size range, recycled pulp capacity cost ($485/ton), gap former vs Fourdrinier cost per inch width, and belt vs pneumatic chip conveyor electricity. Not loaded: the energy-efficiency measure catalogue (Sect. II-III; savings, $/MMBtu capital from Staudt 2010, paybacks) goes to _measures.csv; sector emission totals, black-liquor properties, CHP fleet counts and similar go to _other-values.csv. Nearly all numbers are reprinted from Kramer et al. 2009 (LBNL ENERGY STAR guide), Larson et al. 2003 or Staudt 2010 and flagged in notes; the report adds no original technology data.

(1) Many costs lack a price year ($600/kWe turbine, $0.011/kWh, $485/ton recycled pulp, $38/ton shoe press, $75 million CHP case); others carry mixed years (1996, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2003, 2006, 2008). (2) Cost basis rarely stated; 'per ton' costs do not say whether per ton of annual capacity. (3) 'ton' is used without saying short or metric in Sect. III (Table 1 distinguishes them). (4) CHP performance given as E/T ratios, not heat-to-power, and without efficiencies. (5) Tomlinson furnace efficiency 65-70% given without heating-value basis. (6) Several savings are case-study absolutes (MMBtu/yr, $/yr) without plant size, so they cannot be normalised. (7) Staudt 2010 capital costs are per MMBtu (of boiler heat input presumably) without saying per hour or per year.
